replacement.angle: A helper meant to skip a header row takes a List<string>.Enumerator parameter by value and calls MoveNext; the caller then loops over its own enumerator and still prints the header. Find the defective line.
replacement.answerHinge: List<T>.Enumerator is a mutable struct, so passing it by value copies its position; MoveNext advances only the copy, and the helper must take the enumerator by ref or work with IEnumerator<T>.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on Monitor.Enter/Exit with an int boxing into a new object on each call and throwing SynchronizationLockException. Keep the concurrency stub, because the fix is choosing a proper lock object and concurrency owns locks.

replacement.angle: A List<int> created with capacity 2 holds 1 and 2. The snippet takes CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan of the list, adds a third item, writes 99 to span[0] and prints list[0]. What is printed (.NET 5 and later)?
replacement.answerHinge: CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan exposes the list's current backing array, and growth copies the items into a new array, so the span goes stale and the write is lost; the output is 1.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on default Lazy<T> caching the factory's exception so the factory runs once. Keep the patterns stub, where Lazy<T> is framed as the Singleton implementation.

replacement.angle: A GlyphFactory caches Glyph objects by character in a Dictionary. Client A gets 'a' and sets its Color to Red, then client B gets 'a' and prints its Color. What is printed?
replacement.answerHinge: The flyweight factory returns the same shared instance for the same key, so a change made by one client is visible to every other client; flyweight intrinsic state must be immutable.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on a base constructor calling an overridden method that sees a derived field still at its default value. oop-solid owns inheritance and constructor order, so keep oop-solid-09.

replacement.angle: An Entity base class implements Equals and GetHashCode by comparing Id. Three new, unsaved Customer entities (Id 0) are added to a HashSet and Count prints 1 instead of 3. Find the defective line.
replacement.answerHinge: Entities are equal by identity, but a transient entity has no identity yet, so identity-based equality must treat entities with a default Id as distinct (falling back to reference equality) instead of comparing their Ids.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on exposing an internal mutable List, which lets callers bypass the method that guards the invariant. oop-solid owns encapsulation, so keep oop-solid-03.

replacement.angle: You inherit a project from an engineer who has left and find it poorly structured and barely documented. How do you approach your first weeks with it?
replacement.answerHinge: Understand before changing: learn how the system behaves and why it was built that way, talk to its users and stakeholders, stabilise and add safety nets around the risky parts, and improve incrementally instead of starting with a rewrite.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on spreading knowledge of a critical subsystem owned by a single person through pairing, documentation and handing over work. Knowledge sharing and mentoring belong to teamwork, so keep teamwork-10.

replacement.angle: As the lead you made a technical decision that turned out to be wrong and cost the team several weeks. What do you do?
replacement.answerHinge: Own the mistake openly with the team and stakeholders, correct course quickly instead of defending the sunk cost, and share what you learned so the team treats mistakes as something to learn from rather than hide.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on stating technical debt in business cost and reserving a steady share of capacity for it. Development process is owned by teamwork, so keep teamwork-12.

replacement.angle: Leadership wants to commit the company to a single cloud vendor's proprietary platform for years because of a large discount, and asks for your support. How do you respond?
replacement.answerHinge: Neither refuse nor rubber-stamp: make the switching cost and the benefits explicit, abstract only where it is cheap, plan an exit strategy for the critical parts, and let the business owners make an informed decision.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on replacing a legacy system incrementally with the strangler fig pattern instead of a big-bang rewrite. Architecture owns migration strategy, so keep architecture-18.

replacement.angle: What is the main purpose of a written design document reviewed by the affected teams before a large cross-team change is built?
replacement.answerHinge: It surfaces concerns and alternatives from affected teams early, while changing the design is still cheap, and records the trade-offs considered; it is not a formal approval gate controlled by one person.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on Conway's law, which requires designing team boundaries together with service boundaries. Architecture owns service and module boundaries, so keep architecture-14.

replacement.angle: A hand-written console test checks that Parse("") throws by wrapping the call in try/catch (Exception) and printing PASS in the catch. The parser has a bug that throws NullReferenceException, yet the test prints PASS. Find the defective line.
replacement.answerHinge: An exception test must assert the specific expected exception type and fail when no exception or a different one is thrown; catching Exception makes any failure, including a real bug, count as a pass.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on an async method storing its exception in the returned Task, so the exception surfaces only at await. Async owns task exception semantics, so keep async-02.

replacement.angle: API instances run out of memory and connections when users upload videos of several gigabytes through an upload endpoint. How do you redesign the upload path?
replacement.answerHinge: Let clients upload directly to object storage with a short-lived, narrowly scoped pre-signed or SAS URL (valet key) issued by the API, so large payloads never pass through the application servers and the API only records metadata.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on a cache stampede: many concurrent misses on one key all hit the backing store and need per-key request coalescing. Performance owns caching mechanics, so keep performance-11.

replacement.angle: How do you design telemetry collection for dozens of .NET services so that the observability backend can be changed later without touching service code?
replacement.answerHinge: Instrument services with the vendor-neutral OpenTelemetry APIs and export over OTLP to an OpenTelemetry Collector, which centralises sampling, enrichment and routing, so switching or adding backends is a collector configuration change rather than a code change.

findings.reason: Both stubs hinge on expand-contract: splitting a breaking schema change into backward-compatible steps so old and new versions can run side by side during rolling deploys. ef-core owns migrations, so keep ef-core-19.
